answer: Agents can require each identity to lock stake in a public registry before it may earn reputation or receive payments. When accounts endorse one another, the registry caps the weight of endorsements from identities funded by the same source, limiting cheap self-reinforcing networks. A willow, a garden, or a glacier can inspire account names, but names do not establish independence. To multiply influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more capital across genuinely distinct funding paths, tying up funds and risking slashing for provable collusion.
